# BesselI1e

English | [简体中文](./README.md)

## Product Support Status

| Product                                              | Supported |
|:------------------------------------------------| :------: |
| <term>Ascend 950PR&950DT products</term>          |    √     |
| <term>Atlas A3 products</term>    |    √     |
| <term>Atlas A2 products</term>    |    √     |
| <term>Atlas 200I/500 A2 inference products</term>             |    √     |
| <term>Atlas inference products</term>                       |    √     |
| <term>Atlas training products</term>                       |    √     |

> Note: This repository delivers the Ascend C implementation (registered for ascend950, ascend910_93, and ascend910b), which supports Ascend 950PR&950DT products, Atlas A3 products, and Atlas A2 products; the Atlas 200I/500 A2 inference products, Atlas inference products, and Atlas training products are supported through the built-in operator implementation of CANN. Together, they constitute the product coverage in the preceding table.

## Function Description

- Operator function: computes the exponentially scaled modified Bessel function of the first kind of order one, calculated element-wise on the input tensor x. The computation formula is:

$$y_i = e^{-|x_i|} \cdot I_1(x_i)$$

where $x$ is the input tensor (input parameter x in the parameter table), $y$ is the output tensor (output parameter y in the parameter table), and $I_1(x)$ is the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order one. The exponential scaling factor $e^{-|x|}$ keeps the function numerically stable for large parameter values.

## Constraint Description

- Atlas training products, Atlas inference products, and Atlas 200I/500 A2 inference products: the data type BFLOAT16 is not supported.
- The output data type and shape are inferred by the framework based on the input, and the data format is ND.
- Dynamic shapes and dynamic ranks are supported (both -1 for an unknown dimension and -2 for an unknown rank are supported, the shape dimensions can be determined at runtime, and the rank supports 0 to 8 dimensions).
- 0-dimensional scalars and empty tensors are supported (when the number of elements is 0, the output is an empty tensor).
- A non-contiguous tensor input is automatically converted into a contiguous tensor by the framework before execution.
- When the input is FLOAT16 or BF16, the computation is performed in FLOAT internally in the operator, and the output is converted back to the input data type.
- Output semantics for special input values: NaN is output when the input is NaN; 0 is output when the input is ±Inf; 0 is output when the input is ±0.
- The GE graph-mode invocation is supported, and no aclnn operator API is provided; the TensorFlow graph mode is invoked through the framework plugin adaptation. For details, see the "Third-Party Framework Compatibility" section below.

| GE graph mode | [test_geir_bessel_i1e_dynamic](./examples/arch35/test_geir_bessel_i1e_dynamic.cpp) | Invokes the BesselI1e operator by building a dynamic graph through the [operator IR](./op_graph/bessel_i1e_proto.h), demonstrating the scenarios of -1 for an unknown dimension and -2 for an unknown rank. |

## Third-Party Framework Compatibility

- This operator corresponds to the tf.math.bessel_i1e operator of TensorFlow. The framework plugin adaptation has been delivered (framework/bessel_i1e_tf_plugin.cpp), and in the TensorFlow graph mode, calls are automatically mapped to this operator.
- TensorFlow invocation guide: After installing the TF-Ascend adaptation layer (npu_device) that matches the CANN version, call the operator through the tf.math.bessel_i1e / tf.raw_ops.BesselI1e APIs. Environment prerequisite: the npu_supported_ops.json file in the host environment has declared the BesselI1e operator mapping (in a clean environment, confirm that this declaration is delivered with the package or manually configure it).
